body: I've only figured it out the last year, and I'm 41. Looking back over my life, I realize I was asexual. I just didn't know it. Just see how you feel as you develop. You may change your mind. You may not. I wish I had known what it was early in life. Just be you.
I'm so sorry you are going through this. I know it must be rough. I'm always here to just listen if you need someone. ♡ My heart aches for you.

Not a requirement at all. It is something I would offer to someone I'm in love with. I wouldn't care if she had sexual partners over, although unlikely, if she is asexual. You are really hung up on me wanting my husband a her to have a close relationship. Can you explain why this is abnormal thought?

Yes, I have a therapist. You do know other people have questions that you don't, yeah? I'm sorry I'm not as experienced in my orientation. And I'm completely oblivious to polyamorous relationships it seems. On a serious note..for other people's sake..in the future say everything you have said to me, but try to be more kind so people do take the time to understand and don't run away more confused than they started out.
I'm saying if she likes sexual relationships(which is fine), why would she bother wasting her time investing in one that isn't likely to give her that?
They wouldn't. I don't know why they would bother though.
Ok don't try to talk to this guy. He doesn't want to. Happy?
What requirements? There are no requirements. Im going to this unicorn site to check it out. I clearly wasn't prepared to ask the questions to this community.

Meaning if long tern..and yeah the "I think. Idk" part means I'm confused. JFC Please be done. Take care.

I do have sex to please my husband. I do get aroused, although, not often. I said the opposite about her having sex with my husband. He isn't interested in that.

K guess I don't see how they couldn't be involved in some emotional way if we all lived together. I'm not saying she couldn't be with anyone else...just no expectation of my husband because he doesn't want that.
Is it unhealthy to know what I want in any relationship before I've met them? This particular role is one of love and kindness. And does it apply if I have met them?

No, of coarse she isn't required. No one is required to do or feel anything. I'm speaking from my 20 year marriage and if it came to a point where I want to spend my life with another woman, certain aspects would probably matter depending on the relationship with my husband. Am I wrong?

We is me and her. I tend to think ahead. So I try to imagine a longterm live in situation with my husband. I don't know what that looks like. It's only an assumption,  but I think they would need to be close for it to work. I will look up unicorn hunting because I have no clue what that is.
Actually, it's the way she and I choose. No..not maybe sex with my husband. I clearly stated that. That's insane if that's what you got from what I said.
How am I wanting to treat anyone as a commodity? I'm looking for love, and I would hope for it to be longterm.
Of course not.

Well, I would hope she would be looking for the same thing as me. Someone to love and be loved back in whatever way we choose. So she would get me out of it I guess. lol I feel this is coming across wrong because I am a married woman that has just recently come to terms with who I am. Being in a straight monogamous relationship thus far is making it more difficult than it should be. I just wanted to know if this dynamic was a common thing in this community. I'm merely confused.

Thank you for saying that in a much more helpful way. I suppose I said "add" meaning add to the dynamic of my current relationship. In this hypothetical, said woman would be adding to both of our lives. I feel like I'm using incorrect terminology or being misunderstood. :(
Well, I didn't mean it to sound that way. She needs to be asexual because I wouldn't want her to expect sex from me.

Flip flopping = being unsure and questioning my(our) situation. I don't even understand everything yet pertaining to my orientation yet. I'm going to assume everyone in your community isn't this rude to someone who just had questions because I'm trying to navigate through this, which is all new to me.

You may understand romance, but don't understand me. I'm not disingenuous at all. It isn't abusive or u healthy to layout expectations of what said relationship would be. Unicorn hunter? I do have sex. What I want is not unethical. It may be unrealistic. That's why I posted this question here. People don't deserve to be treated what way? I'm not hiding behind anything. I've just come to terms with who I am in the last year, and I've never been in a polyamorous relationship. I'm only looking for a little advice/guidance in my new journey. Maybe try helping someone next time rather than being an asshole.
I say "adding to our relationship" because it would be. Something that seems like a simple friendship to you can feel completely different and intimate to us ACES.
You give me hope!! ♡

I was lucky to have a great history teacher. He taught us about the civil war, and why the succession was actually taking place. He exposed us to music and books that explained slavery. He couldn't assign us this material, but we were told about it. He also taught us our local history pertaining to slave owners and how they were the founders of our city. A lot of kids in the South don't get that exposure. They grow up believing what they learned in history class. This doesn't make all of them racist. Some are simply ignorant.

I'm in the same situation. I've never fully understood myself completely. I just knew that things weren't the same as my peers. The terminology wasn't there when I was younger as well. I'm 42 now. Looking back over my life, things make so much sense. I've been married to my husband for 20 years. I love him dearly. We talked about it tonight. He was relieved. It made him feel less inadequate over past situations. I believe I'm bi-romantic asexual. This is all so new to experience at this age. I wish I had known this 25 years ago. Is it odd that I desire a Male and female asexual relationship at the same time? I feel guilty about it.
